$comment: Vacation package ideas, with placeholder imagery from Unsplash.
These are starting points for a conversation, not inventory. No packaging
supplier is connected to this site, so nothing here carries a price, a
departure date, a named hotel or an availability claim — every one of
those would be fabricated. What each entry does carry is the shape of the
trip: where, how long, what board basis, and what a package for it
normally includes. All of that is true of the destination rather than of
`bundles` is the honest bit. It says whether a package usually beats
booking the flight and the room separately for that kind of trip, and two
of the six say it often does not. A list that recommended itself six
times out of six would be an advert.
Every alt was written after looking at the frame. Swap the urls for
licensed files under public/images and nothing else changes.

packages.title: A week all-inclusive on the Cancún hotel zone
packages.bestTime: December to April, outside hurricane season
packages.summary: The strip of beach between the lagoon and the Caribbean, where most of the cost is the board basis rather than the flight — which is what makes it bundle well.
packages.note: The classic case for a package: board is the bulk of the bill and operators hold contracted rooms along this coast.

image.alt: A serene tropical white sand beach with gentle turquoise Caribbean waves under a clear sky.

packages.title: Seven nights diving the Cozumel reefs
packages.bestTime: May to September for the clearest water
packages.summary: An island built around the reef wall off its western shore. Dive packages are sold by the operator rather than the hotel, so they sit outside the bundle and are worth pricing separately.
packages.note: Bundle the flights and room; book the diving direct with the operator once you are there.

image.alt: A scuba diver beside a reef wall with a dense school of yellow and silver fish filling the left of the frame.

packages.title: Nine nights island-hopping in Palawan
packages.bestTime: November to May, the dry season
packages.summary: Limestone karsts, hidden lagoons and a lot of boat time. Long-haul with a domestic connection at the end, which is exactly the kind of routing worth having one organiser responsible for.
packages.note: The domestic leg is the reason to bundle — a missed connection on two separate tickets is your problem, on one it is not.

image.alt: Crystal clear turquoise water surrounding tropical island overwater bungalows and lush palm trees.

packages.title: A week among the Dolomite lakes and passes
packages.bestTime: June to September, or December to March for snow
packages.summary: Mountain hotels that still quote half board as standard, and a region that genuinely needs a car. The rental is the part most people forget to price.
packages.note: Ask for the car in the same quote. Adding it afterwards at an Italian airport counter is how this trip gets expensive.

image.alt: Majestic jagged alpine mountain peaks illuminated by morning light above green valleys.

packages.title: Six nights in Tokyo
packages.bestTime: March to May, or October to November
packages.summary: A long flight and a city where the hotel is the smaller half of the cost. Bundling helps less here than the marketing suggests, and we will tell you if it does not.
packages.note: Worth pricing both ways. If you hold airline miles or status on this route, booking the flight separately usually wins.

image.alt: Tokyo Tower glowing vibrantly against the evening city skyline and dusky purple sky.

packages.title: Four nights in Paris
packages.bestTime: April to June, September to October
packages.summary: The trip a package is least likely to win. Short stay, short flight, and thousands of hotels — which means choice matters more than bundling does.
packages.note: We will quote it as a package and as two separate bookings, and tell you which came out lower.

image.alt: Ornate Parisian architecture along the river Seine leading towards historical landmarks at sunset.
